prediction.beta: New mode in testing — predict BTC's 5-minute direction. Prices, settlement rule and taker fees follow polymarket.com.
prediction.title: BTC 5-minute prediction
prediction.targetTip: Chainlink 60-second time-weighted average price (TWAP) at the moment the round opened; this is Polymarket's price to beat. Settlement uses the 60-second TWAP at the close: at or above it is Up, below is Down.
prediction.upTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going up. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.downTip: Probability price: 50¢ = the market gives a 50% chance of going down. Higher price, stronger conviction.
prediction.estPayoutTip: Right prediction: every contract settles at $1. Payout = amount ÷ probability price; the fee is charged on top of the amount.
prediction.feeTip: Polymarket taker fee: shares × 7% × price × (1 − price). Most expensive at 50¢ (1.75¢ per share), cheaper toward the extremes.
prediction.estProceedsTip: What you receive at the current sell price, after fees.
prediction.mySharesTip: Contracts you hold; each is worth $1 if the prediction is right.

jev.title: Jev predictor
jev.intro: Jev bets on BTC's 5-minute up/down market like a player: every 15 seconds after the open it looks at the market and, when flat, decides to buy UP, buy DOWN or wait; when holding, it decides to keep the bet or sell. Code only blocks clearly bad buys and sizes each bet by Jev's confidence.
jev.pnlLabel: Total PnL · settled bets, after fees
jev.scoreDetailsSub: Did Jev's read make forecasts sharper? · {{n}} samples
jev.brierExplain: At every checkpoint the three chances of UP are checked against the result: UP counts as 1, DOWN as 0, and we average (chance − result)². 0 is perfect; 0.25 is what always guessing 50% gets.
jev.brierHow: Watch Momentum-adj. against Math: lower means Jev's momentum read helped; lower than Market too means it beat the market. The lowest in each row is orange.
jev.calibration: Calibration: does 70% come true 70% of the time?
jev.calibrationExplain: The momentum-adjusted chances are split into five bands, and each band shows how often BTC actually finished UP. In the 60%–80% band, roughly seven in ten should have gone UP. The bar is the actual share, the tick is the band's average forecast; the closer the bar's end is to the tick, the better.
jev.guideAction: The first line is what actually happened this time (Buy UP / Buy DOWN / Sell / Hold / Stay out), how much was staked, the time, and how many seconds after the open.
jev.guideChoice: "Jev picks Buy UP · confidence 76%": the option Jev likes most and how sure it is. It only buys at {{act}} or more; below that it does nothing. While holding, Jev is not asked to buy or sell, only about the move.
jev.guideMomentum: "The move: still pushing": Jev's read on the move since the open — still pushing, no lean, or giving back.
jev.guideUpChance: The three "Chance of UP" numbers estimate the same thing — will this window finish above the target price — in different ways:
jev.guideModel: From how far BTC is above the target, how many seconds are left, and how much BTC has been moving lately. Code uses it as the fair price to judge whether UP or DOWN is expensive, and to decide when to sell a position.
jev.guideJev: Math, pushed further along the move or pulled back by Jev's momentum read. It is only scored, to see whether Jev's read makes forecasts better; it does not trade.
jev.guideMkt: Derived from the UP and DOWN prices in the order book. With UP around 67¢ and DOWN around 35¢, the market thinks about 66% UP.
jev.guideCompare: When Math is well above Market, UP looks cheap by the math; the other way round, DOWN does.
jev.guideFold: Routine wait / keep rows are folded; use "Show all" on the right of each window. Click any row to see Jev's confidence in every option.
jev.guideQuestionsTitle: What Jev is asked each time
jev.q1Title: Does the move still have legs?
jev.q1Desc: From the path since the open and the last minute of takers and large trades: is the move still being pushed, going nowhere, or being given back. Scored only; it does not decide trades directly.
jev.qEntryTitle: Bet now, and on which side?
jev.qEntryDesc: Asked when flat. Jev reads the clock, BTC's tape, flow and odds, and buys only when one side looks cheap. Whether a side is cheap is computed by code from the fair price; Jev only uses the last minute, takers and large trades to veto it. It acts at {{act}} confidence or more; code blocks the buy unless that side is cheap by at least {{minEdge}}¢ and its ask is inside {{minAsk}}¢–{{maxAsk}}¢. While holding, Jev is not asked: code sells when the bid, net of fee, is {{sellEdge}}¢ or more above fair value, otherwise holds to settlement. After selling it can buy again in the same window.

notice.NOT_CHEAP: Blocked: {{side}} is not cheap by {{minEdge}}¢ or more
notice.EXPENSIVE: Blocked: {{side}}'s ask is above the math fair price
notice.NO_BALANCE: Blocked: not enough in the game wallet
notice.STALE_BOOK: The order book has not updated for {{sec}}s; Jev was not asked
